content:
Victor Alvarez: trying to lock down the “required VPC endpoints” list for Private alpha so we can stop bikeshedding in module + installer docs.

Assumptions:
- customer may have *zero* public egress
- installer + control plane components need to come up without NAT
- we want the smallest set that avoids support tickets

What do we call REQUIRED vs OPTIONAL for ADR-0128? (ECR, S3, Logs, STS, SSM?)

Irene Choi: +1. We need to be explicit bc if we say “optional” Support will still get paged.

In infra view:
- ECR (api + dkr) is required if we’re pulling images from ECR (we are)
- S3 gateway endpoint is required if we rely on S3 for artifacts (charts, etc) OR if ECR pulls transit via S3 (which it does)
- CloudWatch Logs endpoint depends on log sink (CW vs S3). But we should pick a default.

Marcus Lin: security hat: don’t call something “required” unless we’re willing to enforce/validate it and document endpoint policies.

But also: “no egress” installs are the riskiest from a support standpoint. If we don’t require the endpoints, we need to clearly say “NAT required” alternative.

My concerns:
- STS: lots of AWS SDK flows assume it even when you think they don’t
- SSM: nice-to-have but gets pulled into break-glass access patterns; also increases blast radius if we don’t do policies

Kevin Osei: +1 on STS being surprisingly required. Also, if we use CloudWatch Logs as default sink, we need logs endpoint (`logs`). If we use CloudWatch metrics, also `monitoring` (are we?
)

Allison Grant: on observability: for alpha, we’re not depending on CloudWatch metrics for core functionality. Logs are the big one.

We can allow:
- CloudWatch Logs (interface endpoint) OR
- S3 (gateway) as log sink

But we should make *one* of them required, not both.

Ethan Park: installer angle: we should be strict on whatever the installer assumes.

Current installer does:
- pulls images
- writes some install artifacts to S3 (or reads them depending on mode)
- uses AWS auth chain (assume-role often)

If we do a “private-only” path, I’d rather we say required endpoints: ECR api/dkr + S3 + STS.

CloudWatch Logs: only required if customer chooses CW logs. If they choose S3 logging, we can avoid `logs` endpoint.

Benji Okafor: +1. From code, the failure mode we saw in the lab was:

```
Error: failed to refresh cached credentials, no EC2 IMDS role found, and STS endpoint not reachable
```

(when people block egress + no STS endpoint)

So STS should be in the “required for no-egress” list, otherwise folks will assume it’s fine.

Nina Petrova: question: are we considering VPC endpoints for Route53 / DNS? Some customers don’t have outbound DNS and rely on resolver in-VPC.

Irene Choi: DNS: we’re not doing “Route53 endpoint” per se, but we *are* relying on AmazonProvidedDNS and/or Route53 Resolver rules.

I’d keep ADR scope focused on interface/gateway endpoints and have a separate section “DNS prerequisites” (private DNS enabled on endpoints, resolver in-VPC, etc).

Victor Alvarez: ok, so candidate list:
REQUIRED (for private/no-egress):
- com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.api (interface)
- com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.dkr (interface)
- com.amazonaws.${region}.s3 (gateway)
- com.amazonaws.${region}.sts (interface)

OPTIONAL:
- com.amazonaws.${region}.logs (interface) (if using CW logs)
- com.amazonaws.${region}.ssm + ssmmessages + ec2messages (interface) (break-glass)

Anything else we’re missing? KMS?

Marcus Lin: KMS: only if customer is using CMKs for encrypting whatever we create in S3/Logs/etc. But our terraform modules shouldn’t silently require that.

We should document: “If you enable CMK encryption for CloudWatch Logs or S3, add KMS endpoint (`kms`) or allow egress to KMS.”

Also endpoint policies:
- ECR endpoints: restrict to required ECR repos / account
- S3 gateway: restrict to the artifacts bucket(s)

If we’re not ready to ship tight policies, at least ship stubs + guidance.

Kevin Osei: +1. We can include policy JSON inputs with sane defaults = allow-all for alpha, but doc should say “tighten before production”.

(And Security should sign off on that phrasing.)

Allison Grant: for CW Logs, also call out log group naming + retention. But endpoint list-wise, agree it’s conditional.

Benji Okafor: installer preflight can check:
- DNS resolves `api.ecr.${region}.amazonaws.com`
- can hit STS
- can access S3 via gateway route table

We should align ADR list with what preflight actually validates.

Irene Choi: +1 please do NOT require SSM for alpha. It turns into a policy review rabbit hole w/ some enterprises.

But we can recommend it for operations if they want Session Manager instead of SSH.

Victor Alvarez: what about ECR public? (some people asked)

Marcus Lin: we should explicitly say “no ECR public”. If customer tries to pull from public registries in no-egress VPC, that’s out of scope.

Ethan Park: agreed. Private alpha assumes images hosted in customer’s allowed registry path via endpoints (ECR). If they want to mirror to Artifactory etc, that’s a separate guide.

Nina Petrova: NAT vs endpoints: ADR should state both supported topologies:
- no egress + endpoints (preferred secure)
- controlled egress via NAT/proxy + fewer endpoints (supported but less deterministic)

But for modules we’re building the endpoints path.

Victor Alvarez: proposal for ADR-0128 language:

REQUIRED (alpha, endpoint-only / no public egress path):
- S3 gateway
- ECR api + dkr interface
- STS interface

REQUIRED *if* CloudWatch Logs sink:
- Logs interface

RECOMMENDED (ops):
- SSM + ssmmessages + ec2messages

CONDITIONAL:
- KMS interface if enabling CMKs for endpoints/logging/artifacts

I’ll update ADR draft + module README.

Marcus Lin reacted with :thumbsup:

Kevin Osei: works. add note: private DNS for interface endpoints must be enabled unless customer has custom resolver strategy. otherwise we get weird “endpoint exists but still tries public hostname” issues.

Irene Choi: also call out that endpoints need to be in the *right subnets* (private/isolated) and security groups allow 443 from node subnets.

Victor Alvarez: yup. Will capture under “Implementation notes” in ADR and link to module outputs.

Ethan Park: once ADR is merged, please drop the final list in ENG-4823 + installer preflight runbook. We can make preflight errors more explicit: “missing STS VPC endpoint” vs generic network failure.

Victor Alvarez: ack. pushing ADR updates today. Will paste link here when ready.

---

Victor Alvarez: updated ADR-0128 draft with endpoint list + rationale + conditional sinks. Also added a section on endpoint policies and a clear “no public egress” vs “NAT/proxy” split.

Link: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0128+-+VPC+endpoints+required+for+Private+installer

Please review comments by EOD.

Marcus Lin: reviewed. left 2 comments:
1) move “allow-all endpoint policy defaults” behind an explicit variable w/ scary warning
2) add “STS required” callout in the troubleshooting section (common failure)

Kevin Osei: reviewed +1. also suggest we explicitly mention S3 gateway needs to be attached to *every* route table used by private/isolated subnets (customers miss one AZ and it flakes).

Allison Grant: added note: if CW Logs selected, confirm they have log retention configured (we’ve seen default = never expire).

Victor Alvarez: thanks all. will incorporate and mark ADR as Accepted once those edits are in.
